segments.text: Welcome to BxLens. Observability for BoxLang, built for the developer who has a ticket, and needs the cause. This is the demo application. Everything you are about to see is real.
The demo is a small shop with a control panel. Every page creates one kind of problem, so there is always something to find.
Start with the bar. It sits on every page, and answers one question. What happened in this request?
The strip shows the status, the time, the memory, and the queries. Open it, and the timeline lays out every template and every query, with exact timings.
Here is a classic mistake. Ten orders, eleven queries. The queries tab lists the repeated statement, and the exact line that ran it.
Outgoing calls fail in many ways. A timeout, a rate limit, a gateway error, a host that does not exist. Each one is listed, with its status and its time.
The request tab shows what this one request cost. The processor time, and the memory it allocated.
A caught exception still counts. The bar opens on the problem, by itself.

card.s: The whole server at a glance

segments.text: Now the console. One page for the whole server. The overview shows requests, errors, response time, and what needs your attention first.
At the top, the servers. This one is live. Two more are saved in their own folders. One of them is struggling, with high heap, failing tasks, and a deadlock.
Every request is kept. Filter by address, by status, or by tag. ColdBox requests have their own filter, and each row shows its event.
Open one. This checkout is slow, and the issues explain why. A repeated query, a slow template, and a slow outgoing call.
The same list carries security notes. Missing headers, and cookies without safe flags.
The timeline shows every span. Templates, queries, and outgoing calls, each with its own color. Click a row for its details.
Open every section. The queries, with their parameters and the line that ran them. Exceptions. Outgoing calls. Messages, and timers.
Then the request itself, with its headers, and the scopes, with secrets redacted. The built in functions it called, and the runtime, with the cost of this one request.
A ColdBox request knows even more. The event, the route, the layout, and every view. This one rendered a partial fifteen times, and BxLens says so.
In flight shows what is running right now, longest first, with its thread and its queries so far. Open it when the server feels stuck.

card.s: Errors, runtime health, queries and calls

segments.text: Errors are grouped by cause, with counts, and a sample with its stack. Secrets are removed before anything is stored.
Open a group for the stack, the request, the tags, and every event. Resolve it, and BxLens tells you if it comes back.
Reports give the percentiles, the status codes, and the slowest addresses.
Boards turn the same numbers into charts, so a trend is easy to see.
Now the runtime. This pool is saturated. Two threads, a growing queue, and health notes that say what to change.
Scheduled tasks. One is failing, with its error and its stack. One is slow, and one overlaps itself.
Datasources. Every connection is held, and the next query has to wait.
The queries page ranks every statement of every request. The slowest, the most repeated, and where each one runs.
The HTTP page does the same for outgoing calls. Each endpoint, with its failures counted apart from its successes.
Caches shows every cache, with its hits, its misses, and its entries.
Logs lists every file in the BoxLang logs directory, with its size. Pick one, and it tails live.
Filter by level, search the text, or download the file. No terminal, no ssh.
The system page is the machine under BoxLang. CPU, load, memory, disk and network, live, with the share that belongs to BoxLang.
The CPU, core by core, and the context switches.
Memory shows what is used, what is cached, what is still available, and whether the machine is swapping.
Disks shows how full each location is. The logs, the store, and the temp folder, with warning and critical levels.
Network shows the connections, the interfaces, and the retransmits.
The JVM page starts with what needs attention. Here, two threads are deadlocked.
Memory shows the heap over time, every memory pool, and the rate of allocation. A heap dump is one click away.
Garbage collection. The time spent, the longest pause, each collection as a bar, and the reason each one ran.
The Threads tab names both deadlocked threads, and the lock each one waits for. Below, the pools, the blocked chains, and snapshots to compare.
Classes and JIT. The classes loaded, the code cache, the compiler, and the direct buffers.
And the web server. The worker threads, the traffic, and what is queued.
The overview shows runs, success, run time, tokens and cost. A failing tool is flagged, with the agent that uses it.
Agents. Five agents, each with a mini report. The slowest agents, and the tools that fail most, are ranked on top.
Open the coordinator, and see how it is composed. Its model, its tools, and its sub agents.
Runs lists every run. Agents, model calls, and MCP calls, with their time, their tokens, and the request that started them. Filter for failed, slow, or delegated.
Open a run, and the trace nests the sub agents, each tool, and each model call.
Open a failed run, and see which tool failed, and after how long.
MCP. The servers this application hosts, with their requests, their failures, and their limits. And the servers your agents call.
Models. Calls, latency, tokens and cost for each model, and the agents that use it.
Cost. The spend per day and per run, by model and by agent. Nothing is guessed. A model without a price adds no money.
Registries. Every agent, tool, skill and MCP server that bx-ai knows about.
Settings. Choose how much of each prompt and answer is kept, set the alert limits, and enter your prices.

card.s: The Box Agent for your server

segments.text: Meet Lensy, the box agent for your server. Ask in plain words, and it calls the same tools the console uses. In this video the model is a mock with scripted answers. The tools are real.
Start with, diagnose this server. Lensy runs a health sweep, then looks at the errors and the executors.

Three critical findings. Two deadlocked threads, named. A saturated executor. And a datasource with every connection in use. It also points at the most frequent error, a task that cannot reach the prices API.
Then ask about a page. Why is checkout failing? Lensy finds the latest request, and opens it.
It finds the exception, and ties it to the exhausted connection pool. From a question to a cause, in one chat.
The server selector looks at any server, or at all of them at once, with the numbers added up.
The ColdBox page shows the application as BxLens sees it. Its composition, its modules, its schedulers, its caches, and its findings.
Watchers shows every file watcher, with its events and its errors.
And applications lists every application the server knows.
Back in the demo, three support tickets. A slow checkout. Payments that fail one time in four. A site that slows down over time. Each one has a reproduce button, and BxLens has the answer.
Take the payments ticket. Reproduce it, and the errors page shows one new group. About a quarter of the requests, and the gateway's answer in the sample.
BxLens. Find the cause, not just the symptom. Learn more at bxlens.boxlang.io, and run this demo yourself.
